--- title: "Large VAT (ICMS) debts: distance structure (Figure 3.5.18) and K-means with many initialisations" description: "K-means with 100 initialisations per k on the top 1%, no 2026: main solution k = 4 (author's decision, IMP-13), with k = 2 to 8, elbow, silhouette and HDBSCAN as diagnostics." date: 2026-10-23 jupyter: python3 --- **Data:** the legal-entity-only VAT (ICMS) extract of paper EDA v1 (subsection 1.3), `extracao=2026-03`. **Main base:** top 1% of CDAs by value in the **December 2025** snapshot, with payments up to 31/12/2025 (no 2026). **Comparison base:** the paper's, with the March 2026 snapshot and all payments. **Status:** exploration. **Main solution: k = 4, by the author's decision (IMP-13, 27/10/2026).** k = 2 to 8, elbow, silhouette, hierarchical clustering and HDBSCAN are kept as diagnostics. The subsection draws no substantive conclusions from the groups. ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` scikit-learn 1.9.1; seed 2026; 100 initialisations per k; k = 2 to 8 ``` ::: ::: ## Question and analysis plan **Question.** Do the large VAT (ICMS) debts (top 1% by value) form 2 or 4 stable groups? The silhouette of the paper's hierarchical clustering (subsection 3.5.19) pointed to k = 2. In the research discussion 4 groups were mentioned, from the elbow (the criteria table below shows where the curvature is largest). **Plan (set before looking at the result):** | Item | Choice | Why | |---|---|---| | Unit | Legal-entity VAT (ICMS) CDA in the top 1% by value in the snapshot | Same base as the paper (3.5.1) | | Variables | 6 numerical: log of value, age, recovery, time to first payment, number of payments, share paid under programmes (PEP 2019, Acordo Paulista 2024). 3 categorical: origin, status, court filing | The same as the paper (3.5.17) | | Nulls | A null time to first payment (never paid) takes the age, as in the paper. The others have no nulls | Keeps comparability | | Scaling in the K-means | Numerical variables divided by their range and categorical ones one-hot × 1/√2: each variable contributes at most 1 to the squared distance | It is the scaling of the Gower distance used in the paper. The paper's median/IQR scaling leaves recovery and number of payments (IQR = 0) on the raw scale, and the number of payments reaches 257 | | Method | K-means (Lloyd, k-means++) with 100 initialisations per k, keeping the one with the lowest cost (inertia) | K-means stops at local minima that depend on the starting point. In scikit-learn ≥ 1.4, `n_init="auto"` with k-means++ runs **a single** initialisation | | Alternative | Hierarchical (average linkage) on Gower, the paper's method | Direct comparison with the paper's k = 2 | | Criteria for k | Elbow (curvature of the minimum inertia), silhouette (Euclidean and Gower), stability across seeds (ARI), size of the smallest group | No single criterion decides | | Reproducibility | Seed 2026 + 1000·k + s; silhouettes on the paper's same subsample of 5,000 CDAs | | **Definitions.** *Inertia* = sum of the squared Euclidean distances from each point to the centre of its group. *Silhouette* of a point = $(b-a)/\max(a,b)$, where $a$ is the mean distance to its own group and $b$ the mean distance to the nearest neighbouring group; the mean ranges from −1 to 1. *ARI* (Adjusted Rand Index; Hubert and Arabie, 1985) measures the agreement between two partitions: 1 is identical, 0 is what is expected by chance. ::: {#tbl-bases .cell tbl-cap='The two top-1% bases.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Distance structure (Figure 3.5.18, corrected) **What was wrong with the paper's chart.** In the paper's principal components (PCA) panel, the first component is dominated by the **number of payments**. This variable stays on the raw scale because its IQR is zero (more than 75% of CDAs have no payment; the exact figure is in the figure's "How to read"), so almost all points pile up at PC1 ≈ 0. In addition, the colours of "declared" and "other" were two almost identical shades of teal. **What was corrected:** the PCA is now computed on the same scale as the Gower distance and the K-means (range and one-hot), the three origins get clearly distinct colours and the table shows the explained variance and the loadings. The t-SNE is still computed on the Gower distance of a subsample of 5,000 CDAs. The three panels use the same subsample. ::: {#cell-fig-b518 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {#fig-b518 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Top 1%, December 2025 base, subsample of 5,000 CDAs. Columns: PCA as in the paper (median/IQR scaling; horizontal axis in log), corrected PCA (Gower scaling) and t-SNE on the Gower distance. Rows: all origins and each origin with at least 5 CDAs. Shade = CDAs per cell (50 × 50 grid, log scale); grey outline = all origins (DADOS-14: no point per CDA). ::: ::: ::: {#b518-como-ler .cell execution_count=4} **How to read.** Each column is a projection and each row shows only the CDAs of one origin, in the same window as the column; the shade is the number of CDAs in the cell (darker, more CDAs) and the grey outline is the total, to compare where each origin is concentrated. In the paper's PCA, PC1 is almost only the number of payments (88% of the top-1% CDAs have no payment and are stacked at the minimum), so the axis is in log of (PC1 − minimum + 1). Base: declared 4,951, assessed 18,299, other 3 CDAs. Other has fewer than 5 CDAs and gets no row of its own (nor outline): showing the position of so few CDAs would mean showing individual CDAs. ::: ::: {#tbl-pca .cell tbl-cap='Explained variance and the three largest loadings (in absolute value) of each component, paper\'s PCA and corrected PCA.' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

This explains an ARI close to zero with the K-means. **How to read:** the k = 2 × k = 4 cross-tab shows whether the 4 groups are subdivisions of the 2 (each column falls almost entirely in one row) or cut the base another way. The ARI between the bases says whether the partition changes when the 2026 months are removed. ## What not to conclude ::: {#criterios-k-texto .cell execution_count=18} - No criterion decides k alone, and they do not point to the same k. On the December 2025 base, the largest curvature of inertia (the elbow) is at **k = 3** (0.240, against 0.042 at k = 4); the minimum inertia falls 35.1% from k = 2 to k = 3 and 17.0% from k = 3 to k = 4. The K-means silhouette is highest at k = 4 in both metrics (Euclidean 0.681; Gower 0.664); that of the paper's hierarchical clustering, at k = 2 (0.537). The silhouette favours a few well-separated groups and the elbow shows where the cost gain diminishes. The main solution is k = 4, by the author's decision (IMP-13); these criteria are kept as diagnostics. ::: - K-means minimises squared Euclidean distance. The paper's Gower uses absolute differences. So the partitions of the two methods can differ even with the same scaling. - The range is dominated by a few extreme values (recovery above 100% and more than 200 payments), which compresses the variation of the majority. A transformation such as log(1 + x) would change the results. Left as an open question. - Groups describe profiles. They are not causes of recovery nor collection rules. ::: {#cell-cache .cell execution_count=19} ::: {#cache .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}
